summary: Learn data clean rooms, federated analytics, contracts, and privacy controls for trusted collaboration. Explore the course and enrol.
lede: Data clean rooms and federated analytics offer architectural patterns for analysing data between organisations while controlling access, purpose and disclosure. This course is for data governance, privacy, security and legal professionals who plan and oversee these collaborations, with practice in mapping data flows and risks, designing identity and output controls, and documenting agreements, audit evidence and implementation plans.
audienceIntro: This course suits professionals responsible for making cross-institutional data collaboration lawful, secure, technically feasible, and explainable to executives or oversight bodies.
prerequisites: You should have working exposure to data governance, privacy management, information security, legal review, enterprise architecture, or programme delivery. No programming is required. You should be able to describe a cross-organisational data use case and bring a non-sensitive example of a data flow, contract issue, or collaboration challenge. Advanced cryptographic methods, AI-assisted matching, and federated architecture are taught at conceptual and operational application levels rather than production-engineering levels.
topics: Statistics & data analysis (SPSS, Stata, R, Python)
